newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares rebound as U.S. rate fear quelled.
newsitem.headline: German shares rebound as U.S. rate fear quelled.

text.p: German shares, already sturdy despite Wall Street's overnight tumble, rebounded strongly in afternoon trade on Friday as worries over an imminent U.S. interest rate hike eased.

The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade in the 30 blue chip DAX shares, ended the day up 36.47 points, or one percent, at 3,404.29 points. That was some 45 points ahead of the DAX index's steady mid-afternoon close at 3,359.29 points.
The breakthrough followed a report showing weaker-than- expected U.S. producer prices and capacity utilisation for February, which sent European and U.S. shares shooting higher.
"Just when we were settling down for the weekend, all hell broke loose," a Munich dealer commented.
Selective buying interest had already buoyed German shares through the day, dealers said, although volumes were modest.
Chemical shares rebounded from lows hit this week after disappointing news from Hoechst AG that it did not plan to list its HMR unit.

And Daimler-Benz AG got a major boost after a well-received meeting with analysts at Goldman Sachs on Thursday and news of plan to set up a traffic navigation joint venture with Deutsche Telekom, ending IBIS trade up 3.75 marks at 131.70 marks.

Sports retailer Adidas AG also outperformed, continuing to profit from upgrades following its release of results earlier in the week. The shares surged nearly 11 percent to an all-time high close of 195.90 marks in late electronic trade.

Engineering company Mannesmann AG ended the day with only minor losses after a bullish earnings forecast limited the damage caused by talk of a series of analyst downgrades on its stock, amid worries about the cost of its telecoms activities.
The shares ended the session down 6.45 marks at 640 marks, well off a low of 614 marks.
After a week of precipitous gains and falls on the DAX, prices are now back more or less where they were a week ago.
"We are clearly in a period of extreme volatility. We are going to have to get used to it," said one Frankfurt dealer, noting that the DAX also saw a low Friday of 3,321 points.
A key options expiry deadline next week looks likely to spark more volatility and was already affecting some prices, dealers warned.
But many also said there were no major danger signals for the DAX at present, with domestic investors in particular still loath to take part in any sell-offs.
"Think of it this way -- the dollar is in our favour and interest rates here are still relatively low. We don't have as much to worry about as the U.S. right now," said another Frankfurt dealer.
